whatMatters: Guests are full, entertained, and informed.
Suppliers are full, hydrated, and well-coordinated.
The couple is well-informed and worry-free on the day.

logistics.question: Who is our on-site point person on the day, and what’s their number?
What time can suppliers start ingress, and will each supplier get a set arrival slot?
Where do suppliers unload, and is there a time limit at the drop-off point?
Where should supplier vehicles park, and how many slots are there?
Is there a holding area where suppliers can stage equipment and rest between sets?
How many power outlets are there and where? Is there a generator backup, and who do suppliers send their power needs to, by when?
Where will supplier crew eat, and what time are meals served?
Will there be a water station for supplier crew, and where?
Are there venue rules suppliers must follow (e.g. no nails or tape on walls, sound limits, open-flame or fireworks rules)?
What’s the venue’s cut-off time for pack-up and egress?
How’s the mobile signal at the venue, and is there Wi-Fi suppliers can use?
When is the coordinators meeting, and which suppliers should attend?

rain.question: If it rains, where does the garden ceremony move?
Where do the cocktail hour stations go if it rains?
Where is the candle ceremony held if it rains?
Who makes the fireworks call in bad weather, and by what time?

dressCode.staff: Neat and professional: all black, or black with beige. Closed shoes, nothing flashy.
dressCode.camera: Elegant and formal: suits, gowns or dressy outfits in black, dark beige or light beige. You will appear in photos and videos.
dressCode.avoid: Please avoid white, ivory and cream.
dressCode.cameraWho: Host, coordinators and team leads, officiant, musicians and bands, and anyone running a guest-facing station (bars, coffee, tarot).
dressCode.staffWho: Setup and kitchen crew, lights and sound techs, photo and video team, hair and makeup, and runners.
